items.q: Is Klaviyo a good fit for a business that isn't an online store?
items.a: Not usually. Klaviyo prices and designs itself around active customer profiles built from purchase and engagement data, and its own about page describes it as a B2C CRM built for consumer brands, with integrations into commerce platforms such as Shopify and WooCommerce. A business without that kind of transaction data, a B2B consultancy billing a handful of retainer clients, or a local service business with a short client list, ends up paying for profile-based, behavior-driven segmentation it has too little data to use well. Klaviyo fits best where a real, growing customer list already exists: an online store, an agency running client lists, or a freelancer with an engaged subscriber base. If your contact list is small and mostly static rather than growing from live storefront traffic, a flat-fee email tool built for simpler lists is usually the better starting point.

items.q: Does Klaviyo integrate with ecommerce platforms besides Shopify?
items.a: Yes. Klaviyo's own plan details list more than 350 integrations, and both Shopify and WooCommerce are named directly as connected commerce platforms on Klaviyo's pricing and marketing pages. Those integrations are what let Klaviyo bill by active profile in the first place: connecting a store feeds it order and browsing events it turns into segments and automated flows, rather than relying on a static list uploaded by hand. Klaviyo also lists integrations for channels and tools beyond ecommerce platforms specifically, though this record only verifies the ecommerce side that matters for pricing and fit. If your store runs on a platform other than Shopify or WooCommerce, check Klaviyo's own integrations directory before you commit, since a missing native integration means building the connection yourself or through a third-party sync tool instead.

items.q: What do I get by upgrading from Klaviyo's free plan besides higher sending limits?
items.a: More than just headroom. Klaviyo's help center says paid accounts can remove Klaviyo's own branding from email footers and sign-up forms, something every free account carries by default, and get ongoing email and chat support instead of the 60-day, email-only window free accounts get after signup. Paid accounts can also turn on custom hosted pages, where customers manage their own subscription preferences under your branding rather than Klaviyo's, and Klaviyo's highest-tier accounts are automatically assigned a dedicated onboarding specialist or customer success manager. None of that shows up if you only compare sending limits side by side. The cheapest paid Email tier is $20 a month for 500 active profiles, and for many small accounts the branding removal and better support alone are worth crossing that line before sending volume forces the decision.

items.q: How hard is it to cancel Klaviyo or move my data elsewhere?
items.a: It depends which of three options you pick, and Klaviyo's help center is specific about the difference. Downgrading to free keeps your data and most features, just capped at free-plan limits. Cancelling one paid plan, SMS, for example, turns off that plan's features (an SMS step in a flow stops sending) but leaves the rest of your data alone. Closing your account is the only option that deletes everything, and Klaviyo's own instructions say to export campaign analytics, flow analytics, profiles and templates first, since none of it can be recovered afterward. Cancelling immediately instead of at the end of your billing cycle also forfeits the rest of that paid month with no refund. Klaviyo does publish its own guide for migrating to another email or SMS provider. Account owners or admins can cancel a plan or downgrade to free, but only the account owner can close the account entirely.

items.q: Which businesses should look at a different email and SMS platform instead of Klaviyo?
items.a: Businesses without much purchase or engagement data to segment on, and businesses that want one flat monthly bill rather than several. Klaviyo's pricing model rewards accounts with real transaction history: a connected Shopify or WooCommerce store, an agency managing client lists, or a freelancer with an engaged subscriber base. A business with a small, mostly static contact list, or one that wants Composer, Customer Hub, Social Marketing, Reviews and SMS folded into a single price rather than billed as separate add-ons, will likely find the bill out of proportion to what it actually uses. Buyers in that position often compare Klaviyo against Kit, which has no SMS product and starts well below Klaviyo's entry tier, or ActiveCampaign, which bundles a CRM with email and also scales by contact count. Mailchimp is another common comparison: its Standard plan costs $135 a month for 10,000 contacts, against Klaviyo's $150 at the same size.

items.q: What kind of customer support does Klaviyo actually include?
items.a: It scales with what you pay. Free accounts get email support only for the first 60 days after signup, then fall back to Klaviyo's Community and Help Center with no direct line to a person. Any paid Email plan adds ongoing email and chat support on top of that, according to Klaviyo's help center. Klaviyo's highest-tier accounts are automatically assigned an onboarding specialist, a customer success manager, or both; smaller paid accounts instead get access to Klaviyo's Academy courses, live training sessions and Community rather than a dedicated point of contact. If faster, prioritized responses matter to you specifically, Klaviyo sells that separately: a professional support package starts at $500 a month, and an enterprise support tier starts at $1,800 a month, both quoted through Klaviyo's sales team rather than shown as a fixed price.
